old.name: Ichthyoskala Keratsiniou
old.teaser: Greece's largest fish auction, sold by the crate before sunrise
old.text: Greece's largest fish auction has run at Limani Irakleiou since 1965: the whole Aegean catch lands here nightly. Trawlers and gri-gri boats tie up under floodlights while auctioneers chant prices over crates of red mullet, gavros, cuttlefish and squid; buyers for every Piraeus taverna and Athens fishmonger bid before sunrise. Walk to the ichthyoskala mid-morning and you meet a hosed-down concrete floor — a working quay, not a food hall. Know your species and haggle by the crate.
old.meta: START midnight · liveliest before dawn, winds down ~06:30 · wholesale, cheapest fish in Attica, sold by the crate · Limani Irakleiou, Keratsini

old.name: Central Market of Piraeus
old.teaser: A half-empty shed ringed by century-old refugee food houses
old.text: The covered shed at Agia Triada stands half-empty under a new bioclimatic canopy (2025), but read 'the market' as the two blocks around it, not the building. After 1922 the quarter came to resemble Anatolia — Smyrna shopfronts, three rows of fish stalls; along Gounari and Tsamadou, Armenian and Asia Minor houses still cure pastourma, pull phyllo and roast nuts within 200 metres. Come on foot, mid-morning, on a weekday — most stalls shut Sunday.
old.meta: HOURS mornings to mid-afternoon · most stalls closed Sunday · budget to moderate · Dimosthenous & Lykourgou, Agia Triada

gastronomy:Avakian.group: The curer, the phyllo and the sweet

old.name: Avakian
old.teaser: Four generations of Cappadocian pastourma, cured by hand
old.text: Aram Avakian, a refugee from Kaisareia in Cappadocia, reached Palia Kokkinia in 1922 and cured his first pastourma on his rooftop, then opened a market stall. Four generations have never stopped — fenugreek-crusted air-cured beef, garlicky soutzouki, kavourma preserve — worked by hand in the Stoa Politou arcade off Gounari, where the family moved when the old market was demolished in 1967. Cut paper-thin, the fenugreek rim reads red; a little carries a whole plate.
old.meta: HOURS market mornings · closed Sunday · by weight · Dimitriou Gounari 21–23, Agia Triada

gastronomy:Vourloglou.group: The curer, the phyllo and the sweet

old.name: Vourloglou
old.teaser: Hand-pulled phyllo the port's tavernas buy in
old.text: Brothers Kostas and Dimitris Vourloglou carry an Asia Minor pastry craft rooted in Vourla, near Smyrna, in the basement of Tsamadou 1, reached through a discreet door and worked since the late 1960s. Feather-thin phyllo, shredded kataifi and bougatsa come off the bench still floured — better sheets than most tavernas in Piraeus buy in. A working counter, not a café: buy and go, there is nowhere to sit.
old.meta: HOURS market mornings · closed Sunday · by weight, inexpensive · Tsamadou 1, Agia Triada

provisioning:Mastronikolas.group: The curer, the phyllo and the sweet

old.name: Mastronikolas
old.teaser: The galaktoboureko the whole port measures against
old.text: Made on the same Kallipoli spot since 1909, when it opened as a galaktopoleio — the family kept its own sheep and delivered milk, yoghurt and butter around the lanes of Pasalimani. Founder Panagiotis Mastronikolas' grandsons Giannis and Panos still run it: semolina custard in crisp syrup-soaked phyllo, brought warm, plus kataifi, rizogalo and sheep's-milk yoghurt in glass jars. A no-frills old dairy-and-sweet shop — come for the galaktoboureko, not the decor.
old.meta: HOURS Mon–Sat 08:30–22:00 · Sun 09:00–22:00 · a slice, a few euros · Karaoli Dimitriou 68, Kallipoli

gastronomy:Mandragoras.group: The spice sacks, the roaster and the ship's store

old.name: Mandragoras
old.teaser: Walls of open sacks, from mountain oregano to Greek saffron
old.text: Fotis Vasilopoulos, who started work at eight in a Nafplio grocery, founded Mandragoras in 1955 and has held Gounari since 1963. Walls of open sacks: wild mountain oregano, Greek red saffron weighed from the sack, sun-dried tomatoes, pulses, hand-cut regional pasta, barrel olives. A superyacht chef and a neighbourhood yiayia queue for the same oregano here — a cook's first provisioning stop. Not a supermarket grab: dense, weigh-and-wrap, go with a list.
old.meta: HOURS Mon/Wed/Sat 08:00–16:00 · Tue/Thu/Fri 08:00–20:00 · closed Sun · by weight · Dimitriou Gounari 14–16, Agia Triada

gastronomy:Assos Xiroi Karpoi.group: The spice sacks, the roaster and the ship's store

old.name: Assos Xiroi Karpoi
old.teaser: Almonds and pistachios roasted behind the counter
old.text: The Armenian Ovakimian family, refugees who carried the roasting craft from Asia Minor, have roasted nuts in-store on Tsamadou since 1948; third-generation Agop and his brother Dikran keep the drum turning — almonds, pistachios, candied ginger, roasted chickpeas, dried fruit from every corner of Greece. Everything comes off the roaster warmer and crisper than any packaged nut in the city. The smell of hot almonds on Tsamadou is the market's oldest sign.
old.meta: HOURS market daytime · closed Sunday · by weight · Tsamadou 15A, Agia Triada

gastronomy:Dakoutros Marine.group: The spice sacks, the roaster and the ship's store

old.name: Dakoutros Marine
old.teaser: A four-floor chandler — the world a galley is provisioned beside
old.text: A four-storey ship chandler working since 1981 in the dense nautical-supply district north of the quays that gives Piraeus its identity as Greece's great port. Not a food shop, but the world a galley is provisioned beside: ropes, anchors, fenders, safety gear, stainless fittings, nav lights and marine paints in bulk. The chandler streets behind the quays are as much the city's terroir as any taverna — where a captain buys an anchor and a cook restocks the stores.
old.meta: HOURS weekday business hours · Saturday morning · trade pricing · Antiploiarchou Vlachakou 13 & Gravias
